sentences.text: The home secretary has declined to specify how much scrapping her plan to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait longer to qualify for permanent settlement will cost.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: Shabana Mahmood had originally proposed doubling the wait from five years to 10 for most migrants, with some facing a 15-year wait, which the Home Office suggested could save £10bn.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: Under revised plans, some foreign care workers will wait five years and others will be able to seek a five-year extension, in what the Tories have called a "U-turn".
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: While not detailing the cost of the revised plans, Mahmood told the BBC the state would still save "billions" because workers in other sectors would have to wait longer.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: In March, the Home Office said , external the net lifetime cost of care workers and their adult dependants expected to settle between 2026 and 2030 was estimated at £10bn under existing rules.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: Mahmood was proposing to delay settlement for this cohort in response to concerns over record post-Brexit net migration figures under the previous Tory government - dubbed the "Boriswave" by critics.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: Following a backlash, Mahmood announced on Monday that care workers who arrived in the UK before May 2025 and earned at least £25,000 a year would continue to qualify after five years, alongside some other groups.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: Foreign care workers who do not qualify for the five-year settlement will be able to apply for a new five-year visa, and then seek settlement.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: Indefinite leave to remain (ILR), also known as settlement, gives a person the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like and apply for benefits if they are eligible.

sentences.text: They can also use it to apply for British citizenship.

sentences.text: Asked about the cost of her revised plans, the home secretary told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the detailed costs would be published when her department puts the changes before Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: She said the changes overall represented "savings in the billions" to the Department of Work and Pensions in people not claiming benefits.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood refuses to detail cost of revised settlement plans

sentences.text: "The reason for that is the cohort that was most likely to fall upon the state is that cohort of care workers not doing care work at the moment - if they'd settled at five years, many more of those would have gone on to claim benefits.

sentences.text: "That will now not happen because they will not be settling at five years - those individuals get a second chance to make that contribution that they originally came to make," she told Today.

sentences.text: The midterm elections are under way in the US, as voters take part in a ballot that could have a major impact on the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Americans will choose members of Congress, which is made up of two parts - the House of Representatives and the Senate.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Elections take place every two years, and when they happen in the middle of the president's four-year term of office, they are called the midterms.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: A key task of Congress is to create and pass federal laws - laws that apply nationwide.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: The outcome of the midterms will decide which political party - Trump's Republicans or opposition Democrats - controls Congress and how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: The results are also seen as a measure of how happy people in the US are with the president's performance so far.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Follow live updates on US midterm elections All 435 members of the House - the lower chamber of Congress - will be elected.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: They serve fixed terms of two years.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: The House is commonly where proposed laws are introduced and debated.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Meanwhile, 35 of 100 seats in the Senate, the upper chamber, will also be up for grabs.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Senators serve six-year terms.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Among other jobs, they approve or block proposed laws that have been received from the House.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Governor contests in California, Florida, Georgia and Michigan will be among the most closely watched.
sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.article_title: A simple guide to the midterms

sentences.text: Derbyshire Police admitted its officers went outside their powers and acted unlawfully in December 2022 A couple have been awarded £9,000 in damages after police admitted its officers unlawfully entered their home and assaulted them nearly four years ago.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Andrew and Sabrina Fearn had a house party in their home in December 2022.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Earlier, Sabrina had called police and officers attended before leaving.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: They then returned, believing someone was injured inside and wanted access.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Sabrina refused, but officers forced entry and used physical force on her, according to legal documents.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Andrew then stepped in before "unnecessary force" was used on him.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Both were arrested and charged with assaulting an emergency worker, but their trial was halted when police admitted the forced house entry was unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Andrew and Sabrina, from Alvaston in Derby, pursued a civil claim against the force, and the case has now been settled for £9,000, the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) said .
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: According to the legal claim submitted by the couple, a gathering at their home ended when they discovered one of the guests had a knife.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Sabrina called the police, which attended and then left shortly after.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: But soon after, several officers returned wanting to gain entry, believing someone was injured inside and needed urgent medical attention.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Sabrina, 31, refused to let police in, saying the party had finished and no guests remained.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: She tried to stop police from entering her house, before officers forced entry and used physical force on her.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Andrew, 40, stepped in to protect his wife, fearing she was being hurt, before "unnecessary force" was used on him, according to the legal papers.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Extracts from police bodycam footage describes Andrew being held by the throat against a wall, while Sabrina was held by the neck as officers forced entry.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Andrew was warned he would be Tasered if he did not comply, was sprayed in the face with an incapacitant spray, handcuffed, taken away in a police van and held for 15 hours.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: According to the LDRS, as the couple made physical contact with officers during the incident, both were arrested and charged with assaulting an emergency worker.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: However, the pair were found not guilty in the middle of their trial, after police gave evidence to admit the forced entry to the home was unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: Sabrina said: "It has caused an awful amount of stress.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: My mental health was so bad that whenever anyone came to my door, I would lock it.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: I have awful PTSD [post-traumatic stress disorder].
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: "If I entered someone's property unlawfully and harmed people, I would be done for assault.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: I would have a criminal record.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: In a statement, the force apologised for the distress caused, and said officers had acted on a "honestly held belief" someone inside may have been injured, but later accepted the legal grounds for entering the property had not been met.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: No disciplinary action was taken against the officers involved, the force added.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: A spokesperson said: "We would like to take this opportunity to apologise for the distress and harm that was caused by this incident.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: "It was later found that, due to the time that elapsed between the initial call and officers entering, that the grounds under section 17 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act were not met and that the entry, and all other matters following it, were unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: "There were also claims, which were not accepted by the force, that the woman was unlawfully arrested, she was not handcuffed or detained at any point and the necessity for arrest was not met due to her suffering a medical episode, during which the officers provided immediate first aid.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: "It was also not agreed that the man had suffered a dislocated shoulder during the incident.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: It was also not accepted that a malicious prosecution had taken place - or that officers were negligent.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.text: "As a force, we always expect the highest possible standards of conduct from our officers and staff.
sentences.article_title: Police admit unlawful home entry and assault of couple

sentences.article_title: Dry and chilly start to November after wet but sunny October

sentences.text: The Greens have been in direct coalition with Labour on a handful of councils, including Sheffield The Labour Party has pulled out of power-sharing agreements with the Green Party in 11 local councils, after the national party adopted a policy defining Zionism as a form of racism.

sentences.text: Labour councillors will no longer be in coalition with the Greens in areas including Sheffield, Warwick and Lewes.

sentences.text: In October, Green Party members backed a motion, entitled "Zionism is racism", which said Zionism was an ideology that supported an "ethnonationalist Jewish State in historic Palestine".
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Israel has denied committing genocide in Gaza.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: The motion also backed a "single democratic Palestinian State", including in modern-day Israel.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Having been backed by party members, the motion became Green Party policy, but it has left senior figures bitterly divided .
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Jewish groups and opposition political parties have condemned it.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told MPs in October that Labour would not partner with the Greens over the "antisemitic" policy.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Labour then issued an ultimatum from Labour's head office to Labour-Green councils, demanding that local Greens disown the motion passed by members at their national party conference.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Green groups were also asked to call on their party's national leadership to reconsider the policy.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Labour said there were local agreements in place in 18 authorities.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Of those, Labour said 11 had not met the criteria it demanded.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: The party said that Coventry City Council does not have a formal arrangement in place and that no such deal will be made in the future.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: It will continue co-operating with the Greens in the West of England mayoralty, where the deputy mayor is a Green member.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said the motion was "imperfect" but has defended its central premise , arguing that Israel's actions towards the Palestinian people are "clearly underpinned by racist ideology".
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: The collapse of co-operation at the local level could impact hundreds of thousands of residents through budgets and policy decisions taking longer to get voted through.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Green and Labour councillors in the impacted areas will now have to seek alternative coalition partners or try to govern as a minority administration.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: In a joint statement, the Green Party and the Local Government Association Green Group said it was "hugely disappointed" that Labour had forced local leaders into "jeopardising successful progressive partnerships that are delivering benefits for residents".
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: One of the biggest councils to be affected is Sheffield, where 25 Labour councillors formed a power-sharing agreement with 20 Green councillors after the May 2026 elections for the Yorkshire city's 550,000 residents.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Responding to Labour's ultimatum, leader of the Sheffield Greens Angela Argenzio did not mention the motion in a letter but insisted local Green councillors "are not antisemitic".
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Argenzio told local Labour representatives they were being "directed by your national party leader" rather than local concerns.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: In a statement on Monday, the council's Labour leader Cllr Fran Belbin said her party would propose on Wednesday that it proceeds as a Labour minority administration.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: "We now feel we are at the end of the road with the joint administration," she said.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: "Our trust in Sheffield Greens is completely broken," she added, accusing them of a "refusal to stand up for Jewish citizens".
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Green group leader in Havant Netty Shepherd accused Labour of "performative politics" and said the end of their coalition would be a "complete disaster for residents".
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: "I am a local government councillor, I worry about people's bins, I worry about generating town centres - foreign policy is nothing to do with my remit," she added.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats are also in partnership with the Green Party in some local councils.
sentences.article_title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row

sentences.text: Last week, the party leader Sir Ed Davey ruled out entering into a national partnership with "any party that is committed to a dangerous and antisemitic policy like the Green Party's".

sentences.text: A seven-month pregnant woman whose unborn baby died after she was discharged from hospital while suffering from a life-threatening condition was told by staff to make an appointment to give birth.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: Danielle Brown, 31, from North Tyneside, said she was devastated to have to return home knowing the baby she was carrying was no longer alive.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: She said no family should be put through the same experience and wants hospitals to offer alternatives for those grieving.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: After she was discharged from hospital suffering with pre-eclampsia, Danielle insisted on returning to the maternity unit as she felt so unwell and was seen by doctors.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: She was told her daughter had died but, instead of delivering the baby, the hospital sent her home and told her to ring to book a slot to give birth.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: Her partner Anthony Miller, 34, described it as "horrible... lying in bed and holding that belly" knowing their baby was not alive.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: The Newcastle Hospitals NHS Trust said it fully accepted "aspects of the care we provided fell short" and offered a "heartfelt apology".
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: Anthony and Danielle were overjoyed to learn they were having a girl Danielle and Anthony had been delighted to learn they were having a baby girl, who they decided to call Maisie.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "I was just over the moon, I couldn't be happier," Anthony said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: But in February 2023, seven months into her pregnancy, Danielle woke up feeling unwell.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: Her face was swollen, as were her hands and feet - all potential signs of pre-eclampsia , external , which can be life threatening to both mother and baby.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: The couple went to the Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital in Cramlington, Northumberland, but medics found problems with Maisie's heart rate and told Danielle her baby needed to be delivered immediately via emergency caesarean section , external .
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "Maisie's heart rate had dropped and a midwife ran in and said 'don't panic, but I need to pull the emergency cord - you're having your baby'," Danielle said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: The midwife told her space was being found for her at the Royal Victoria Infirmary (RVI) in Newcastle and doctors there "were going to do the section", she said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: She was transferred by ambulance but, once in Newcastle, Danielle did not have the operation and was instead put on a ward.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "A consultant came to see me and he said I am staying in hospital until Maisie was born," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: But, the following day, another doctor reviewed her and sent her home.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: A normal scan showed Maisie at 16 weeks Within 24 hours, again feeling unwell, Danielle called the maternity unit and said she was told she probably had a stomach bug.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: But she insisted on being seen.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "When I finally had a scan, the screen was turned away and there was no sound," Danielle said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: She remembers turning to her partner and saying: "I think she's gone." Doctors were unable to find Maisie's heartbeat and they told Danielle her baby had died.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: But instead of delivering the baby, as she expected, Danielle was given a phone number, and sent home.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: She said they told her to "give us a call on Friday morning, and book a slot to come in and have Maisie".
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: At home the couple struggled to cope.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "It was horrible," Anthony said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "Lying in bed and holding that belly, and still being able to feel Maisie but knowing she wasn't alive." Two days later, after 10 hours in labour, Danielle gave birth.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "When Maisie was born the room was silent," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "Seeing Maisie was bittersweet.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: I told her she was beautiful and I loved her.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "It was devastating that my first experience of holding a baby was holding my stillborn daughter." Danielle and Anthony finally held Maisie two days after being told of her death Speaking publicly for the first time about what happened, Danielle said no-one should be sent home still carrying a baby who has died.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "Just take that family and help them.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "When we left hospital, we gave Maisie one last cuddle and kiss and told her we loved her and were sorry things couldn't have been different." After saying goodbye to their daughter, the couple faced further distress.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: To leave the hospital they had to walk past other parents holding their babies.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "We should have been leaving with our baby too, but we were leaving with a memory box," Danielle said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "All the new mums were walking out carrying their babies.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: That will stay with me forever." The couple want every hospital in the UK to provide an alternative way out for grieving mothers, to "make a different route for a parent who has just lost a child".
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "What happened to Danielle and Maisie vividly highlights the human cost of care failings," he said.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "The trust admitted Danielle should not have been discharged on either the 14th or 15th of February 2023.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: Had she remained in hospital, monitoring would have shown the need to speed up delivery and Maisie would have been born alive." An NHS England spokesperson said: "These failings in care are unacceptable and should never have happened.
sentences.article_title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died

sentences.text: "Anyone experiencing the loss of a baby should be fully supported by a specialist maternity team so they can make choices about their care that are right for them." Have you been affected by the issues raised in this story?

sentences.text: Drivers may be offered compensation from lenders ahead of the next legal battle in the car finance mis-selling saga .
sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.text: Regulator the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said it would welcome lenders making settlement offers as long as customers were not given a worse deal than under its proposed central scheme.
sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.text: That scheme is facing a legal challenge, to be heard in February, with resulting compensation unlikely to be paid until late next year.
sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.text: Stephen Braviner Roman, the FCA's general counsel and co-lead on the motor finance project, said: "Fair settlement offers could result in some people getting money sooner.
sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.text: It's clear they want the choice.
sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.text: "Anyone who wants to wait can, and there's no obligation to agree to the offer.
sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.article_title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends

sentences.text: Binance customers withdrew $3.6bn (£2.7bn) of assets from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following what is believed to be the largest hack in history.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: The firm suspended all transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack .
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach but the remaining amount may take longer to source.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: Binance said on X: "Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion." There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: Sunday's net withdrawals account for just over 2% of the $171bn of assets under its management, said Binance.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: The firm said last week that it has reserved more than $6.3bn in funds, to deal with ​the fallout of the attack.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: Funds linked to the Binance hack continue to be laundered, according to Alec Zebrick, senior manager in global services at Chainalysis, which has been working with the firm and governments to get the stolen money back.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: "We continue to see funds being laundered quite actively," he told the BBC's Today Programme.
sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.article_title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack

sentences.text: Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff are facing redundancy as the telecoms firm attempts to save money in the face of billions of pounds of debt and tougher competition.

sentences.text: Airbnb host Lisa says her Welsh holiday let was left 'a complete mess' by a group of guests When Lisa Clewes returned to her Welsh holiday let after a group of guests checked out, she was horrified by the mess.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: Just days earlier, she had met the group in person and helped with their luggage.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: But after a dinner party, the house was left "in a complete mess" with broken glasses, drinks cans on the floor, pans full of food on the table and fish guts left in the garden.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: "It was really unbelievable.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: Had I had another booking the same day, I would have had to cancel or delay check-in," says Clewes.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: She charges a cleaning fee that covers around 75% of the cost of a cleaner and asks guests to empty the fridge, put rubbish in the bins and load the dishwasher.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: The updated guidelines, which apply to bookings made globally from 20 November, state that hosts can now set seven standard house rules and add other "reasonable" requests.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: Clewes says it typically takes cleaners four hours to turn around her three-bedroom property.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: She fears guests leaving more mess could mean hiring extra cleaners and increasing costs – expenses that may ultimately be passed on to her guests.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: The changes have come as a relief to guests like Jessica Newhook, who says she has been faced with lengthy checkout lists, often on top of hefty cleaning fees.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: She booked an Airbnb in Florida for a family reunion of 11 guests and says they had to "leave the property move-in ready for the cleaners", despite paying a $250 (£187) cleaning fee.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: Newhook says the host told them to wash and fold towels, clean the bedding and kitchen, and sweep and mop the floors.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: She was also warned by the host that their behaviour needed to improve or they could be told to leave, because they had left chairs blocking bins.
sentences.article_title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests

sentences.text: "We had rules about everything and it was not relaxing at all." While Newhook likes the home comforts of staying in an Airbnb, she says the combination of relentless rules and rising cleaning fees has taken away much of its appeal.

sentences.text: Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI).

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Other tech stocks, including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble.

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Ian Thomas, chief executive of the City of London Corporation, has been named the UK's most influential Black Briton in this year's Black Powerlist awards.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The 57-year old is the first Black person to oversee the Square Mile's governing body in its more than 900-year history.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The City of London Corporation is an administrative body with responsibility for London's central financial district, headed by its own Lord Mayor.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas tops the 2027 Black Powerlist, which recognises the most powerful people of African and Caribbean heritage in the UK.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The award body said he was "a respected public-service leader with over 30 years' experience in local government".
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Other influential names in this year's top ten include entrepreneurs Emma Grede and Steven Bartlett, as well as actor and filmmaker Sir Idris Elba.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Comedian Sir Lenny Henry has also been recognised, with a Lifetime Achievement award, for co-founding Comic Relief, which has raised over £1.6bn since 1985.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Now in its 21st year, the Black Powerlist celebrates people who have broken through barriers to reach leadership roles, thereby inspiring future generations.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: "It exists to show young people of African and Caribbean heritage what is possible, in fields they might never have considered," said Michael Eboda, the list's publisher.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: As chief executive, he oversees around 5,000 staff with responsibilities including the City of London Police, 11,000 acres of open spaces such as Epping Forest and Hampstead Heath, and advocacy for the UK's financial and professional services sector.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas was born in Sheffield to parents who made the city their home after leaving Jamaica as part of the Windrush generation.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: "They worked incredibly hard and instilled that sense of discipline and respect, and that's the core of how I do business," he said of his upbringing.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Growing up, Thomas aspired to be a footballer and took part in trials alongside Alan Shearer.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Reflecting on his own change of direction, Thomas joked it was about "following dreams and if they don't come true… there's always something else".
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Before joining the City of London Corporation, Thomas served as chief executive of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames where he oversaw public services and a £1.2bn regeneration programme.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: He was appointed a CBE in the 2019 New Year Honours in the wake of the Rotherham Abuse scandal for transforming children's services during his time as strategic director for children and young people at Rotherham Metropolitan Borough Council.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas replaces last year's incumbent, Afua Kyei, the Bank of England's chief financial officer and executive director, and is joined on this year's list by Comfort Ero, the President and chief executive of the International Crisis Group, who takes second place.

sentences.text: Amazon Prime Air is expanding to 500 US towns and cities Nature lover Ashley Schmidt no longer spends much time in her garden, in the Dallas suburb of North Garland.

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They emit this very annoying buzz.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Amazon says it is working to reduce the noise of its drone fleet Schmidt is one of a growing number of people living with the noise of drones dispatched by companies including Amazon and Walmart as they seek to speed up home deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Delivery drone services, not long ago a novelty, are becoming part of everyday life for many people in the US.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Among them, Amazon Prime Air is in the process of expanding deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns, delivering items that fit into a space the size of a shoe box.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also launched to customers in and around Darlington in the north of England.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Smaller drone delivery services are popping up too: in some US cities, customers can order flying treats from their local pizza joint or ice cream parlour.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Even in cities where noise is already a steady part of life, the sound of drones seems to irk in a particular way.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While the steady passing of traffic might blend into the background, the sudden whine of a drone's rotors can pierce the everyday hum.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The sound tends to be "particularly noticeable, even when overall sound levels are relatively low," says Antonio Torija Martinez, professor in acoustic engineering and psychoacoustics at the University of Salford.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Unlike planes, drones operate at low altitudes and may fly directly over residential areas.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They can expose communities that have not previously experienced significant aircraft noise, and who may therefore be more sensitive to changes in their local soundscape," says Torija Martinez.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He points to research showing that people respond strongly to a noise when they consider the source to be "novel, intrusive or frequent".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: People who benefit from a drone delivery service, for example, may be less bothered by the noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The FAA says operators and local community leaders have primary responsibility for addressing any community concerns.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: One startup, Greenjets, set out to tackle both "noise level and the frequency of that noise," as Darren James, future technologies lead at the company, puts it.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The London-based business has designed a propulsion system it claims can reduce drone noise by at least two thirds.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While standard drones use spinning propellers that slice through open air, creating that high-pitched buzz, Greenjets encloses spinning blades inside a pod, to muffle the sound and direct the noise away from the ground.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Its system also quietens things down through slower rotor speed and by using materials that reduce vibration noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Making quieter drones isn't just about keeping the noise down for neighbours who are already sick of airborne deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets' low-noise tech has been used by police and harbour security teams in Germany.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "There are some efforts to reduce the sound of drones.

sentences.text: Sharrow Engineering developed twisted propellers that reduce noise For Detroit-based entrepreneur, Greg Sharrow, it was the challenge of broadcasting a classical music performance back in 2012 that set him on the path to quieter drone design.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He needed to film a violinist from a tricky angle and a drone seemed the only solution – except that it would be far too noisy.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: As a starting point, "I knew that most of the noise from the drone was coming from the propeller, not the motor," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Mohammed Ashim is paid to film his hands at work Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working." He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off." But his customers are getting more demanding.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Now clients are asking for four to six cameras rigged around a person's head to cover the entire scene, not just the hands.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Getting someone to agree to one small camera is one conversation.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Getting them to agree to wearing what's effectively a five-camera headset is a completely different, and harder, one.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We pay more for that tier of data collection because of what we're asking of people." And the industry is becoming more crowded, Agarwal expects dozens more competitors to emerge in India this year.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Shahil Baig expects dozens more firms to start collecting video of workers Why is such data so important?

sentences.text: If you want robots to navigate the real world, they can't just be trained inside computer simulations, argues Manish Agarwal, the founder of Humyn Labs, which collects and processes human-generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Most of that data comes from video, but sometimes collectors wear hardware on their hands and fingers to capture physical contact.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Physical tasks require high-quality signals involving limb movements, fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders and dynamic force application.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Humyn Labs filters the thousands of hours of video supplied by those collectors, selecting the most useful content.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: It's then labelled so the AI knows what it is looking at and packaged in a format that can be used by clients.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "You need to source across a variety of factories, a variety of tasks, in different geographies because if you want to build deployment for US factories or US houses, you'd want environments that are a proxy for that.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Residential houses in India may not be the right context for building a robotics use case for the US." This video can not be played The factory workers teaching robots how to work like humans But are workers collecting data for machines that will one day do their jobs?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment it's too early to tell says Bino Paul, senior professor at the School of Management and Labour Studies at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) in Mumbai.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For some workers AI might be a useful tool, but robots could automate other jobs, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The problem is that, if machines do start to take over, there will be little workers can do about.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "By the time workers realise what they have participated in, things may have gone too far," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Like many others, he wants governments to regulate AI.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "AI cannot be viewed merely as a technical system.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We need to develop a socio-technical system in which ethics is upheld through human agency, ensuring that AI delivers beneficence rather than maleficence." Despite concerns over where AI is heading, money is still being poured into its development.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Some of that trickles down to workers in India, where there is no shortage of workers prepared to wear a camera for a few dollars a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Mohammed Arman has been working in the textiles industry in Bangalore for 10 years.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Garments stitching and cutting.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I know this work so well I could probably do it with my eyes closed.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Cloth, thread, needle, machine after 10 years, your hands just know what to do before your mind even tells them," he says.

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I have a family back home in Bihar, and every rupee I send back matters.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: If someone offers me extra money to wear a camera while I do the exact same work I've been doing for 10 years, I'm not going to say no.

sentences.text: "It doesn't cost me anything.

sentences.text: I'm already doing the stitching, already doing the cutting.

sentences.text: "India's current role in this industry is largely as a supplier of raw material - people strap on cameras, record themselves doing ordinary tasks, and that footage gets shipped off to labs abroad," Agarwal says.

sentences.text: Shabana Mahmood has backed down on two elements Today's announcement has long been viewed in government as a potential political banana skin.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: When the home secretary announced her first version of changes to the settlement system last year, many Labour MPs, including the housing secretary Angela Rayner, voiced their concerns about the plans.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: But there was a feeling that Sir Keir Starmer's government was determined to plough on regardless.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Shabana Mahmood herself repeatedly expressed how important she believed the reforms were.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: But the change of prime minister over the summer gave renewed hope to those unhappy Labour MPs that they could force the Home Office into two changes.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Firstly, social care workers – under the original plans many social care workers would have had to wait 15 years before becoming eligible for settlement.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Secondly, the retrospective nature of the plans – some MPs were uncomfortable at the idea of someone coming to the UK and expecting to be eligible for settlement after five years, but then having to wait longer.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Angela Rayner described that as "un-British" and said the government shouldn't be shifting "the goalposts".
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: She returned to the cabinet under Andy Burnham as housing secretary and chose to repeat those criticisms in an interview during the Labour Party conference in September.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: That was seen as evidence that a debate inside the top levels of government about whether to water down the plans was well and truly rumbling on.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: For all the Labour MPs who wanted a change, there were others, particularly those in Brexit-supporting areas, who wanted the home secretary to stick the course.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Some inside government felt nervous about providing what they saw as catnip to Reform and the Conservatives.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: All of that added up to one of the more difficult decisions that has had to be taken since Burnham walked through the doors of Number 10.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: In the end ministers chose to water down the proposals for care workers – those who arrived before May 2025 and earn at least £25,000 a year will qualify for settlement in five years.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: But the retrospective nature of the plans, the thing Rayner described as shifting "the goalposts", hasn't changed.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Despite that, the majority of Labour MPs pulled their punches when Mahmood made a statement in the House of Commons earlier .
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Perhaps the strongest pushback came from Rachael Maskell, who is no fan of the retrospective element - but others on the left of the party, including John McDonnell and Diane Abbott, were critical without being scathing.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers What are the planned changes to immigration rules?
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Outside the Commons chamber, the mood among Labour folk was pretty similar to what was said from the green benches.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: One would-be critic said that while they personally still had concerns about the plans announced today, they believed the Home Secretary had successfully taken the political sting out of the situation for now.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: They said the campaign by MPs and unions had led to a "big win" on settlement for social care workers, but said they were still expecting to hear from constituents negatively affected by the new rules.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: One Number 10 source praised Mahmood's "take no prisoners" performance in the chamber, argued she had "found the right balance" and said the announcement had gone down as well as could be expected with Labour colleagues.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Of course, the home secretary will still need to deal with criticism from other parties.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Her opposite number for the Conservatives, Chris Philp, accused Mahmood of a significant U-turn.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Philp highlighted a claim she had previously made – that allowing care workers to reach settlement more quickly could cost the UK £10bn.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: The social care workers plans announced today will see around 500,000 people have their path to settlement delayed , that number would have been around 800,000 under the original plans last year.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: In an interview with the BBC, Mahmood wouldn't say what sort of financial burden her watering down would result in.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: She also refused to confirm whether Burnham had directly asked her to water down the plans.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: They are tricky questions that she will have to navigate over the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: But the general view within government is that this is one political hurdle that has been successfully jumped.
sentences.article_title: Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes

sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Neither did thousands of other residents in Homer, Alaska, who later discovered a  start-up called Rainmaker conducted an experiment in that region using cloud-seeding technology.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The company, based in El Segundo California, claims it produced 19 million US gallons of water in the sky in three hours.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: This approach to weather modification, now more than 80-years-old, involves using planes and drones to disperse compounds such as silver iodide into clouds to form ice crystals.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Gravity then pulls those crystals to the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: The technology, though, needs ideal climate environments, such as mountainous or cold regions such as Alaska.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman, the Alaska director of the Center for Biological Diversity, isn't just concerned Homer residents weren't widely alerted to these experiments.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He's sceptical about what was shot into the clouds, and questions how safe it was for both residents and their habitat.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It doesn't appear that there was any downstream monitoring to verify that this silver iodide didn't impact the environment," he says.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Freeman adds, "Having a company come in to do this seeding isn't going to solve our water woes, and it feels like a distraction from solving the urgent issues related to water conservation." Concerns are mounting about the challenges surrounding water security.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in July "our world is using freshwater faster than it can be replenished , external ", which echoes reports noting how the past five years have led to the driest period for global rivers , external in more than three decades.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding technology may be a drop in the bucket, as it doesn't create rainstorms.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: For example, Rainmaker's 19 million gallons equates to around 0.01 inch of rain across 100 square miles.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Nevertheless, more than 50 countries , external are developing programmes to modify the weather and a surge of start-ups are developing systems to create rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: As well developed and promising as this innovative field has become, these businesses continue to face thorny questions on safety and efficacy, leading to novel approaches with both finding the right material to spray into clouds and how they do it.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Augustus Doricko with a Rainmaker drone Augustus Doricko, the founder and CEO of Rainmaker, is quick to answer any questions on the consequences of how his company uses the silver iodide compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: It's clear he's been asked about chemical safety many times.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: He says Rainmaker releases this form of silver at 20 grams per flight, distributed across thousands of square kilometres.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Cloud-seeding sessions have to wait for clouds to form to try to coax them into precipitation.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Their drones are outfitted with silver iodide flares, and when lit the burning atomizes the water particles into a small enough size so they can stay suspended in the freezing cloud for hours, eventually turning into crystals and later rain.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Rainmaker operates in states such as Idaho, Utah, Colorado and areas of the Middle East such as Jordan.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: A year later, silver iodide was found to be more effective than dry ice, which quickly turns into useless gas.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While seeding agents caused more rainfall, they didn't move the needle much.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In fact, sobering statistics point to how patchy this technology can be in what it pours on the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "With the right conditions, cloud seeding squeeze out about an extra five to 10% of precipitation," says Jon Meyer, an assistant state climatologist with the Utah Climate Center.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: What was encouraging, though, for the cloud-seeding sector was a landmark 2017 study that found how silver iodide worked as expected, one of the first reports to observe cloud seeding in action using radar and precipitation gauges.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: In the past several years, Meyer has been encouraged to see more companies such as Rainmaker bring innovation to an old industry.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "Drones [such as Rainmaker's products] present this new avenue," says Meyer, "and they offer a more targeted nature to these clouds we hope will be responsive." Olivia Li is developing an alternative to silver iodide for cloud seeding What is sprayed into clouds may also be undergoing a major shift.

sentences.text: Recast Systems in San Francisco is experimenting with a type of protein made from amino acids found in the soil, says CEO Olivia Li.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: While still undergoing tests at Texas A&M University, this new seeding agent moves Recast away from silver iodide as the go-to compound.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: "It's safe, biodegradable and nucleates ice at a higher efficiency than silver iodide," says Li, whose company currently uses silver iodide to seed clouds in several US states.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Meyer is optimistic this technology's trajectory will only continue to rise.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds
