sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.

sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In adults it causes a similar weakening of the bone called osteomalacia , external .
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Symptoms include fatigue and joint and bone pain.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday says: "It's basically silently eating away at the bones, leaving them softened and prone to breaks." Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I couldn't really see in front of me," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: After taking supplements, Amaka feels a lot better, but she is anxious in case it happens again.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "It was scary and I don't want to experience that again." Uday joins other clinicians and academics who have formed a group - ACT NOW Vitamin D - calling for the threshold at which you are classified as deficient to be raised.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: It would also mean they can treat the deficiency earlier, she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If you don't correct it from the very beginning," she says, "this is going to affect multiple generations." Saskia Reeves-Priestley plays football four times a week - and had no previous symptoms "It's shocking," says Prof Martin Hewison, from the University of Birmingham.

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After divorcing her husband and coming out as lesbian, Mindy co-founded a lesbian commune in Hull before moving to Manchester On one occasion, while Mindy was in hospital after a stroke, a nurse referred to Linda as Mindy's husband.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She said it was not only "insulting", but made her consider what sort of training the staff might have had.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Spotlight on Ageing report says these sort of experiences can also have an impact on the support people receive.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Sarah Wilkinson, research and analysis manager at the Centre for Ageing Better, says after a "lifetime of homophobia and transphobia", older LGBTQ+ people now face the "additional, and overlapping, challenge of ageism".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report , external says older LGBTQ+ people are less likely to have children - someone born in 1950 would have been in their 50s by the time same-sex couples could legally adopt - and that they are more likely to be estranged from their families when compared to their heterosexual counterparts.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report also found more than half of gay and bisexual men aged 65 and above live alone, compared with less than a quarter of heterosexual men.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Bisexual women aged 50 to 64 are twice as likely as their heterosexual peers to live alone.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: It also suggests that only half of gay and bisexual men aged 50 and above definitely agree they would have someone to help them if they needed, 14 percentage points lower than heterosexual men of the same age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman Goodman, 75, came out as bisexual in his late 60s after the death of his wife Marilyn.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The couple never had children, and Norman now has no immediate family nearby to help him with things like hospital visits or housework.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: He says his support system comes in the form of his partner Tony, and a group of friends and neighbours he refers to as his "chosen family".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I'm lucky, I've got great friends and great neighbours, and I know I can knock on somebody's door day or night and I could get help," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman came out as bisexual when he was in his 60s and says he relies on "chosen family" to support him But despite having their support while he's relatively independent, Norman says he worries about the prospect of facing discrimination if he needs more formal care as he ages.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "Hopefully I will maintain and look after myself the best I can, but I've heard horror stories of gay people in nursing homes being treated terribly," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think nurses, doctors, carers should all be trained on how to look after LGBT people." It's the reason behind schemes like Manchester's Kindred House, which are not unusual in other parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There are similar projects in Spain, Sweden, Germany, the US and Canada, but in the UK they are few and far between.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: In 2021, the UK's first LGBTQ+ retirement community, Tonic, opened in London with 19 apartments for affordable rental or shared ownership.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The scheme attracted so much attention, later this year it is set to feature in a Netflix documentary telling the story of one of its first residents, Chek Min-Ong.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After 43 years together, Min, 77, and his late partner Tim, had discussed their plans for a future where one of them would live alone, as Tim's health deteriorated.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Min and his late partner Tim wanted to make sure they lived somewhere supportive when one of them passed away "Tim and I have always had this very open discussion, we wanted to know, when one of us is not here anymore, the other person will have a community and feel safe," Min says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: When Tim died five months after moving into Tonic, Min says his new-found community rallied around him.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It is what [Tim and I] always wanted, that we'd never have to explain ourselves," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "We'd never have to face a question and feel guilty about not telling the full story, or having to lie.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "You're just here, being yourself." While schemes like Kindred House and Tonic are welcomed by Mindy, Norman and Min, the Spotlight on Ageing report warns that, because the older LGBTQ+ population is growing, the demand for specialist services is expected to outstrip supply.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, the number of over-50s identifying as lesbian, gay or bisexual in the UK increased by around a third - from roughly 340,000 to almost 460,000.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There was a 4% rise in the number of heterosexual people aged 50 and above in the same period.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: These numbers are projected to continue to increase as the relatively larger younger generations of people identifying as LGBTQ+ age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.

Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The government has said its vision , external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She said an "explosion" in short-sightedness "cannot be put down to genetics alone".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: It also warned that children with special educational needs are "disproportionately" directed to screen-based learning.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said education technology can provide schools with "very effective learning tools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: But he said such technology was only part of an "overall learning strategy", which also includes classroom discussion and interaction, and that the school day also has  "plenty of non-screen time such as PE, sport, and break times with classmates".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: "We would welcome the development of practical, evidence-based guidance to support the work of schools in the use of education technology," he added.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.

sentences.text: US Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald vowed to pursue all those involved In May 2024, Francis Mogambi arrived in the United States after winning the Diversity Visa lottery, a programme that gives people from around the world a chance to become permanent residents.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Just over two years later, the Kenyan national found himself at the centre of a US investigation into an alleged nationwide scheme to defraud the federal student aid system.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: On 19 October 2026, a grand jury in Nebraska indicted Mogambi on five counts of theft of government money and five counts of aggravated identity theft.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors allege that, between November 2025 and May 2026, he worked with associates in Kenya to steal the identities of US citizens and use them to fraudulently enroll fictitious students in American colleges.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Once the fake students were enrolled, Mogambi allegedly diverted their financial aid payments to himself, keeping 30% and sending the remainder to his associates in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The intended loss in his case was $20,000 (£15,000), according to prosecutors.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Court documents say Mogambi received $2,000 a week and attempted to recruit another person into the scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He allegedly told the individual he needed a business that would allow him to cash larger cheques without paying taxes.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Mogambi was arrested shortly after the indictment was returned and is being held in custody pending trial.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He has not yet commented on the allegations against him.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: His case forms part of a wider US investigation, dubbed Operation Ghostbusters, into the alleged use of stolen identities to enrol fictitious students at colleges and claim federal financial aid that resulted in a loss of $130m in taxpayers funds.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: US authorities say the investigation has so far resulted in five indictments that involved Kenyan nationals, while a further 40 investigations remain open.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Hundreds of people have been affected after fraudsters allegedly stole their personally identifiable information (PII) and used it to access federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The stolen personal information was sometimes sold online for between $4 and $8, with fraudsters targeting low-income Americans who had never had the opportunity to attend college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At a news conference on 29 October announcing the first charges in the investigation, Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald, who heads the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division, vowed to pursue those involved.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "If you steal taxpayers' dollars, if you exploit a programme meant to help students, we are resolved to find you and prosecute you," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department says those behind the fraud use what is described as "super intelligence" to place fake students in classrooms and complete coursework, creating the impression that they are attending college and allowing financial aid payments to continue.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "The goal is to keep the ghost student in school as long as possible.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Semester after semester after semester stealing money from the taxpayers," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: But the consequences extend beyond the financial losses suffered by the US government.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: People whose identities are stolen can find themselves facing unexpected student loan debts, even if they have never enrolled in college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "His identity was stolen, his credit is now at risk, and his name is on the bill," McDonald said, describing the impact on one victim.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He also said that nearly a third of community college applicants in California in 2024 had been identified as fraudulent.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The scale of the suspected fraud is significant.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent Federal Student Aid identification numbers associated with nearly $130m in September and October 2026.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: They recommended that the Department of Education disable them.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The figure represents financial aid associated with potentially fraudulent accounts, not confirmed losses.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "In a flash, the money vanishes, often overseas in places like Kenya," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The investigation has also exposed alleged financial links between the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In September, US officials travelled to Kenya to work with local law enforcement on extraditions, prosecutions and the recovery of money allegedly stolen from American taxpayers.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: With the help of Kenyan investigators, US authorities seized more than $750,000  from a cryptocurrency account belonging to a Kenyan national connected to the wider scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department described it as the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The seizure was not connected to Mogambi's individual case.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In a separate case in Virginia, prosecutors allege that a Kenyan national received more than 700 fraudulent student-aid refunds totalling approximately $1.44m.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At least $1.3m was subsequently transferred through thousands of transactions to accounts in the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in New Jersey, three people have been charged with allegedly acting as money mules in a scheme to obtain more than $1m in federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors say they received the funds through US bank accounts, kept a portion for themselves and transferred the remainder to alleged co-conspirators in Kenya linked to a purported safari company.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: If convicted, Mogambi faces a mandatory prison term of at least 10 years, according to the Justice Department.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Authorities say those convicted will also face appropriate orders for forfeiture of assets and restitution to victims, in addition to any prison sentences.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: New vocational GCSEs will be introduced from 2029 for 14-year-olds alongside existing core academic subjects in England.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The new subjects could include building and construction, business management and finance, and child development.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said there was "no question" that academic learning was at "the core of any education system", but said there was "huge demand" for subjects with more practical elements too.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education unions said the ideas were welcome, but a clear strategy was needed to make them happen.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The Conservatives said the plans risked "throwing away" progress made in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Standards for the new qualifications will be set nationally by the regulator Ofqual to ensure grades are in line with other GCSEs, and will gradually replace other qualifications at this level such as BTec tech awards.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The vocational GCSEs will be designed to allow teenagers to progress at 16 to studying similar courses at college, including the new V-levels , which schools and colleges are teaching from autumn 2027, and T-levels .
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The idea is to create a clear pathway for teenagers into different types of work through a ladder of qualifications.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: But the Liberal Democrats warned the new vocational GCSEs should not become a "pipeline" directing disadvantaged pupils away from more academic subjects.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC she was "not going to oversee a two-tier education system".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: "I want working class, disadvantaged young people to have every opportunity to achieve highly academically," she said.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Asked whether there would be dedicated funding to help schools cover the cost of the new qualifications, she said the government would "work with the sector to make sure this is absolutely deliverable", and that ministers would "make sure any funding needed is made available".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: A new national target for employers to help create 200,000 work experience opportunities for under-16s is also being set by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, as part of reforms to shake-up the education system to better prepare young people for the world of work.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: VCSEs , external , a new style of vocational qualification unique to Wales, will be taught in schools and colleges from September 2027.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Learners in Wales can choose from 15 VCSE subjects including Animal Care​, Nature Restoration​ and Motor Vehicle Maintenance​.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Daisy is taking business studies at BTec Level 2 - this is the kind of subject that could be replaced by a new Vocational GCSE Vocational subjects at 16 currently make up 7% of the entries for qualifications in England and it is up to each school how many subjects with hands-on learning they offer.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Wright Robinson College in Gorton, East Manchester, already offers 10 practical or vocational subjects for study in Year 10.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Daisy, in Year 11, is taking business studies as a BTec Level 2 which she said is giving her "practical experience" and building her confidence to progress to an A-level in the subject.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: This is the kind of subject that may be replaced by one of the new vocational GCSEs.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Many of these existing tech awards have their standards set by the examining organisations, not the regulator.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The standards for the new vocational GCSEs will be national.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Sarjo, also Year 11, already knows she wants to be a flight attendant so she is taking hospitality and catering as a BTec Level 2 alongside GCSEs.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: She said she "learns faster" in the practical subject and most teenagers want to do something they enjoy alongside core academic subjects.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Martin Haworth, executive head teacher at Wright Robinson College, said any new qualifications had to "add value" to what was already on offer and labelling them as GCSEs might help with credibility.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: He said schools would need to recruit specialist staff if the courses and exams were going to be "robust", and it would cost schools money to convert existing classrooms for practical learning.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Sarjo enjoys the practical elements of her hospitality and catering BTec New analysis of school funding by the independent Institute for Fiscal Studies shows the budget per pupil is growing faster than expected, by 9% in real terms between 2025-26 and 2028-29.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: This is partly because of various government top-ups to the budget and falling pupil numbers in some areas.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Economist Luke Sibieta said asking schools to offer more vocational routes would be a "big change" on top of the significant reforms to support for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: He said there was a "big question mark" over whether there were enough people to teach technical and vocational subjects, with further education colleges already struggling to recruit.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The Association of Colleges (AoC) suggested schools worked with them because they could offer "industry standard facilities" and qualified staff.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: David Hughes, from the AoC, said this would help ensure learning was "authentically different to school and properly employment focused".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Daniel Kebede, from the National Education Union, said "sustained investment and resources" was needed to make a success of the new qualifications.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: While Pepe Di'Iasio, of the Association of School and College Leaders, described the government's plans as "well-intentioned", but not making sure schools had the staffing and resources would not remove barriers to young people.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: He welcomed the national push for work experience and said with placements "extremely difficult" to secure, more support was needed from employers.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The existing statutory career guidelines for secondary schools in England already require "meaningful" work experience for 14 to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Employers are now being asked to contact their local careers hub to offer placements.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Laura Trott MP, who is the Conservative Party's shadow education secretary, said she was concerned the changes risked losing the progress England had made in improving standards, and "ripping up the system" could mean "sabotaging young people's futures".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: "Better schools will continue to protect rigorous subjects but disadvantaged children will be steered towards easier routes, lowering expectations for the very pupils who need high standards most," she said.
