sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Campaigners argue this gives renters greater security and confidence to ask for repairs, without fearing they could be evicted if they raise concerns.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Lewis Wilson from the NUS says the legislation has given students more freedom to move out when they want However, greater flexibility for students to leave tenancies also means less certainty for landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The act did introduce a specific ground , external for landlords to evict a group of students at the end of the academic year if they intend to re-let the property to students.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association, says the bigger problem for student landlords is if their tenants choose to move out earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He argues this is a bigger risk for students - who may fall out with their housemates or drop out of university - than, for example, families, who are less likely to want to move out after just a few months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says the end of fixed-term tenancies means student houses could be left empty over the summer after courses finish - or even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He adds that it is now more difficult for student landlords to rent a house for just a few months as they don't know how long the tenants will stay and can't guarantee it will be available for students again in the autumn.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says it's early days for the new legislation and many landlords are taking this year as a test to see how these issues play out in practice.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, he warns that some may choose to increase the monthly rent they charge to cover the risk of their properties being empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: In some cases, he says landlords may even sell up or stop renting to students, reducing supply and pushing up prices.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue Lawes thinks the changes mean many student landlords will put up their rent Sue Lawes, who rents three shared houses to students in Norwich, is worried about the changes.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While Sue says she doesn't want to put up her prices, if her houses end up being empty over the summer because students decide to end their tenancy after their final exams she says she may have to.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She has already brought forward the start of her tenancy agreements to August instead of September to try and reduce the risks of this.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, she says if her tenants move out earlier in the year she would struggle to make a profit, whilst covering costs including her mortgage, council tax and utility standing charges when the properties are empty.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She argues higher monthly rents would mean bigger upfront costs for students and higher overall costs for those who do choose to carry on renting over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue stresses that she supports the aim of the legislation to give tenants greater security and that students should be able to move out if their landlord is not carrying out repairs.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But she wants landlords to be allowed to offer fixed-term contracts to students in line with the academic year to avoid properties being left empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords are going to find it very, very hard to absorb those void periods," she says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords will put prices up and students are going to pay." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

sentences.text: The Bedford School, Mohali, is the newest in at least half a dozen British public schools (elite, fee-paying private schools with a long history), including three of the country's oldest, that have set up shop across the length and breadth of India.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Their expansion comes amid tighter market conditions in China and the introduction of VAT on private school fees in Britain from 1 January 2025.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Since 2023, Bengaluru - India's Silicon Valley and a hub of software and start-up companies - has been home to the prestigious Harrow School, alma mater of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.

sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Shrewsbury School has a campus in Bhopal in central India, while Wellington College has chosen to set up base in Pune, a western city that calls itself the "Oxford of the East" for its well-regarded universities and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Millfield and a few others are reportedly on their way with satellite campuses in the coming years.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: For decades, India has been home to well-established local boarding schools modelled on the colonial British public-school system, serving elite, aristocratic families.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But this market has rapidly expanded with newly wealthy Indian families increasingly aspiring to give their children more global exposure.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "Our international curriculum is quite a driver for many of them," Caroline Pascoe, head of school at Harrow in Bengaluru, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Harrow and Bedford are among the few schools in India that follow an all-through Cambridge curriculum - a global education framework recognised at 10,000 schools worldwide - from primary through to A-levels.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: He said he was also drawn to the fact the school did not have a "VIP culture" unlike many Indian equivalents.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "All kids are treated the same.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Children of ministers and bureaucrats don't get greater privileges," said Singh.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Beyond the growing ranks of well-heeled local families, non-resident Indians who have either returned home after long stints abroad, or those still in the UK or Middle East wanting their children to connect to their roots, are also a significant market for these schools, says Pascoe.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: There is also a house system - a hallmark of traditional British education.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: These quintessentially parochial quirks are blended with local customs such as singing the Indian national anthem every morning or celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi, a major Hindu festival.

sentences.text: Schools such as Harrow in Bengaluru promote extracurricular activities like music and drama While India's growing economic credentials and burgeoning population of newly minted millionaires are a natural tailwind for expansion, this growth is partly being driven by a slowdown in China.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Much of the expansion of British public schools abroad in the past decade was driven by China and Hong Kong - half of the 151 satellite campuses operated by 50 UK schools are situated in these countries.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But that growth has slowed following changes in regulation, and "increased scrutiny, and even resistance, from national governments", according to a 2025 study by the UK-based Private Education Policy Forum ( PEPF , external ) think tank.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: A new 2024 Chinese law that required schools to integrate patriotic education into all subjects further challenged expansion and even led to planned campuses being cancelled, prompting these schools to consider other locations like India and Vietnam, according to PEPF.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Moreover, in the 2024 Autumn Budget, Britain introduced a 20% VAT on private school fees.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Naomi Atkins, founding principal at Bedford School Mohali, says this has forced many private schools to look overseas.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "They are in a desperate situation.

sentences.text: Even those that hadn't previously looked for international expansion are now suddenly active in India," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Well-heeled local families and non-resident Indians are a major target market for British schools in India But India has not been an easy market, she admits.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Most of these schools are set up in partnership with local investors or operators.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: While in the past schools in other countries might have been able to do deals at 10% of revenue - the fee that they would charge the local partner-investor - margins in India may have shrunk to as low as 1% in some cases, says Atikins.

sentences.text: There has also been some over-estimation of the size of the market, she says.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Even though India has nearly 250 million children enrolled in schools, English education is deeply entrenched in the country and competition from local players is much more intense compared with other non-English speaking countries like China, Korea or Vietnam.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: India's per capita income is also far lower and the high price-points of the British schools - which can charge up to £15,000 or more for full boarding - can limit growth.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "I've worked in Indonesia, Malaysia and China but Indians are much more price-sensitive - they like a bargain," says Atkins.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: That is why Bedford Mohali has set its fees at roughly half those charged by other British schools.

sentences.text: But in India, it appears growth is likely to be slow and steady rather than explosive.

sentences.text: The university had a deficit of around £12.5m in the last financial year Staff at Queen's University of Belfast (QUB) have been warned of "difficult decisions" ahead due to the university's finances.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Pay deals with staff, and childcare and gym fees for staff and students are under review while staff car-parking charges are going up.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: The details came in an message to staff from the university's vice-chancellor Prof Sir Ian Greer.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: His message came after the grant paid by the Northern Ireland Executive to universities had a "significant" cut in 2025/26 .
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: According to Greer, the university had a deficit of about £12.5m in the last financial year.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: While the university hoped to reduce that, he said that a combination of cuts in funding from Stormont and a fall in student fee income meant the university had to "control costs".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: There have been tougher visa requirements for international students coming to UK universities in recent years.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: According to the university's annual accounts, the income QUB received from international student fees recently fell by around £5m - from more than £60m in 2024 to around £55m in 2025.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Greer also said that student recruitment income was expected to be around £7m "below target" in the current year.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: He said that the university still hoped to deliver agreed pay deals to staff.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: "However, given the Department for the Economy's position, we have no choice but to keep the position under review," he said.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Ian Greer (left) with former US president Bill Clinton Some other charges, including for staff car-parking on campus are going up.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Costs for university services that staff and students use, like childcare and membership of the university Physical Education Centre (PEC) are also under review and may rise.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: However, plans for a new university heritage and visitor centre , external , to be built in the Quad on the site of the current administration building, are going ahead.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: But there may be more savings measures to come.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: "The University Management Board has agreed to identify approximately £10m of savings this year and, depending on the final position with public funding, further difficult choices may have to follow this academic year," Greer said.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Greer said that due to a cap on student numbers, QUB had turned away "around 500 students who had the grades to attend Queen's".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: The number of local students both QUB and Ulster University (UU) can admit is decided by Stormont's Department for the Economy and depends on available funding.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Current QUB students who use university childcare or the PEC may also face higher fees for the services.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: But Greer said that "the student experience must remain central to our decisions".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: In a further statement to BBC News NI, a QUB spokesperson said that the university was "facing increasing financial pressures arising from reduced public funding, lower student recruitment income and rising costs".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: "Our planned approach is centred on both stability and growth, to secure the university's long-term future while supporting our students and staff," it said.

sentences.text: Erin Bleakley led a wave of protest after having her exam results downgraded A student whose exam results were downgraded during Covid says she still wants answers from education bosses after their decisions changed the trajectory of her life.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin Bleakley's plans were ruined after she was awarded Bs, Cs and Ds in her highers in 2020 after an emergency marking system was introduced.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Despite her results being eventually adjusted, she never got the A grades her prelims suggested she would get and she had to change course.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: As former SQA head Fiona Robertson prepares to give evidence to the Scottish Covid Inquiry later, Erin wants someone to take accountability for what happened.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin (centre) led protests against the exam results algorithm After lockdown came into force in March 2020 and schools were closed to pupils , teachers were instructed by the Scottish Qualifications Authority (SQA) to estimate exam grades for pupils.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: A later review , external found there was no consistency with how this was carried out around the country.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: In June, the SQA then lowered 125,000 of these grades using an algorithm, saying the grades did not tally with the outcomes of previous cohorts at the same schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Public outrage grew when it became apparent that pupils who had gone to schools in deprived areas formed the bulk of students who had their results downgraded from teacher estimates.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Grades were then restored to teacher estimates for those who had been downgraded.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: But by then it was too late for some pupils who had already lost their chance of a specific university course, because they had entered clearing.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Plus, some students were surprised that the restored teacher estimates didn't match  prelim results.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Schools were closed in March 2020 and learning was rushed online Erin, who is from Glasgow, can't forget the moment she opened her exam results in August 2020.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: She'd been studying for six Highers and after getting A grades at prelim, was hoping to study veterinary medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I remember being quite excited," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I didn't think anything was going to go wrong.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: I thought I'd set myself up really well." Then the postman arrived and Erin remembers opening the envelope, receiving three Bs, one C and two Ds.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "My legs buckled beneath me, I remember feeling I just couldn't believe this had happened," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It did not reflect anything that I'd done over the last two years." Erin had never failed a class in her life.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: She said: "I was crying uncontrollably.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: I remember my mum just didn't know what to do and my dad came home from work early.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: It was a horrible experience." The story was repeated on social media and among her school friends.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Then she opened Twitter and saw a post from a private-school pupil from an affluent area who was delighted that despite failing all their prelims, they'd just got five A grades.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I remember thinking, something's not right here," Erin said.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "All of my friends and people I know that wanted to do medicine weren't getting the grades that they got in their prelims." Erin organised a Facebook page and set up a protest in Glasgow's George Square.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It felt like my full life had disappeared in front of me.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: And when I started reading into it, I realised it wasn't anything to do with me.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin's adjusted grades were not enough.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: She pivoted to studying human geography.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin says she still wants answers.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It was a massive injustice that people faced.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: I think I would like to know if anybody in any of these deprived areas was consulted before these decisions were made.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I think there needs to be some sort of accountability in the system.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It has still left an impact on people to this day.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: So I do think it's important, even just for acknowledgement, to take accountability of what happened and what went wrong." Covid and lockdown caused massive disruption to education in Scottish schools The experience set her off on a different path.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: She is now a PhD student at the University of Glasgow, studying environmental research and community work.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Her research has looked into automated algorithms and the effect on lived experiences, looking at decisions about people which have been based solely on statistics.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I've kind of built my full research around making sure that communities are involved in any work that I do because of the inequality that I faced, that a lot of us faced," she said.

sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: It took another four years for its replacement Qualifications Scotland to take over many of its responsibilities.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Critics called the change a "superficial rebrand", especially as the new body has many of the same staff as the old one, but its stated aim is to "reset relationships with learners and teachers" in order to "win back trust".
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: A spokesman for the new Qualifications Scotland agency it was committed to supporting the work of the Scottish Covid-19 Inquiry and continues to engage fully with the inquiry's work.

sentences.text: "It would not be appropriate to comment further while the inquiry is ongoing," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "The SQA developed an alternative certification model in March 2020.

sentences.text: Like a lot of other holidays, food often plays a big part in how people celebrate Halloween, but it can be a more complex to navigate if you have a food allergy - especially if you want to go to parties or take children trick or treating.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: How do people with allergies ensure they can take part in the fun and stay safe?
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: And how can you help make sure that everyone is included in the celebrations?
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara, 15, is allergic to milk and eggs.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "You have to make sure you read every packet of everything, and you couldn't eat anything until you got home so that you were safe and you were sure of what was happening," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: When it comes to Halloween, she said people having more awareness would mean that everyone could be included in the fun.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She says that her friend group really help her by knowing about her allergies and what to do if she was to have a reaction.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Whilst she said it "wasn't easy" or a "particularly enjoyable" thing to do, she taught her group what to do in an emergency situation.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara, 15, went to a Halloween party this week dressed as Daphne from Scooby Doo Ciara carries EpiPens.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: These are adrenaline injections that can help to save people's lives in a serious allergic reaction.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: The 15-year-old explained that Halloween can be a bit more difficult to navigate.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She described how a lot of people are helpful and understanding about allergies but sometimes, "there are other people that just don't seem to fully understand the consequences" of what would happen if she was exposed to what she's allergic to.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Her mum, Claire McGuigan, said she is proud of how well Ciara deals with her allergy.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She explained that parents of children with allergies have all the usual worries but "first and foremost is your allergy".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "As a parent, you carry all that worry and you just hope that they go out and they have a nice time and they come back safe, full of fun, and they can forget about their allergies as much as they can for that night".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "I think having a good circle of friends who understands the allergies is important.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Trying to prevent the harm rather than relying on the rescue medication is really, really important," she continued.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara's mum described the emotional burden on families and called for a national conversation about it.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said people who have children with allergies or have allergies themselves have to do their "best to navigate a whole world that wasn't designed for you".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "I think take your wins everyday that you're safe and that you're happy and don't let it define you.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: You can be who you want to be," she continued.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She believes that with "a bit of careful planning" children with allergies can feel included.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán in his Halloween costume Caolán has just turned 11.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: His mum Colette Donaghy said he does all the "school activities that you could name" and he's "mad into scooting".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán is allergic to nuts, dairy and eggs and has had, in the past, a very serious anaphylactic reaction that resulted in him being in an induced coma in intensive care.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "He has an awareness and a knowledge and probably a risk awareness that many other children of his age wouldn't have," his mum said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She thinks it's important that children with allergies are "understood" but not made  to feel "really different".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán's mum, Colette Donaghy, said giving out individually wrapped sweets to trick-or-treaters could help avoid cross-contamination When it comes to Halloween, Donaghy explained that when Caolán trick or treats, he waits until the end when all the other children have been given their sweets.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Then he will explain to the people at the door that he has allergies and there's only certain things he can have.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: And then, of course, before he would eat anything, we would have to check it," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Donaghy advised giving out individually wrapped sweets to help avoid cross-contamination.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She also suggested looking at alternatives to sweets like fruit or little toys "that don't cost very much".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "There's loads of different options for people and that would take away another layer of anxiety for parents," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Donaghy also explained how some people use teal pumpkins to indicate that a house will offer treats that are suitable for any trick-or-treaters who have any food allergies or intolerances.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Niamh Kennedy, from Food Allergy NI, said everyone should "think ahead" to consider how they can make celebrations inclusive Niamh Kennedy has three children who have food allergies and she is the chair of Food Allergy NI.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: It's a group aiming to build a safer and more inclusive society for everyone affected by food allergies.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said special occasions are often centred around food.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "For families living with food allergies, these celebrations can bring an extra layer of planning and worry that many people never have to think about." She explained that "every item may need to be checked and every situation assessed for risk".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Kennedy suggests that everyone should "think ahead" to consider how they can make celebrations inclusive.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Conservationist Sacha Dench welcomed the ban on lead ammunition A conservationist has welcomed new laws banning the sale of lead ammunition as she warns people are not aware of the scale of the problem affecting wildlife.

sentences.text: Sacha Dench, who lives in Chagford, Devon, is a member of the Lead Ammunition Collective, which campaigned to end the sale of the toxic substance earning the group the RSPB Medal - the charity's highest accolade.

sentences.article_title: Woman who flew with swans warns of lead danger

sentences.article_title: Woman who flew with swans warns of lead danger

sentences.article_title: Woman who flew with swans warns of lead danger

sentences.text: Uganda accuses Peter Elwelu of stockpiling weapons and organising activities against the government Uganda has arrested former deputy military chief and presidential adviser Peter Elwelu over allegations of involvement in activities aimed at destabilising the country.
sentences.article_title: Uganda arrests former army deputy chief stripped of military rank

sentences.text: Acting military spokesman Chris Magezi said Elwelu, whom he described as a "renegade" officer, was arrested on Monday evening and would be charged in court.

sentences.text: The arrest comes days after Uganda's defence chief, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, announced that he had stripped Elwelu of his lieutenant general rank and demoted him to a private.

sentences.text: Elwelu has not commented on the allegations.
sentences.article_title: Uganda arrests former army deputy chief stripped of military rank

sentences.text: Elwelu rose to prominence in 2016 when he oversaw a deadly military raid on the palace of a regional king accused of leading a separatist movement.

sentences.text: Donovan Marx, 50, was attacked during a house robbery on his farm in Ventersdorp, a small town in South Africa's North West province, last Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: Marx was ambushed as he returned home, shot and stabbed and had his ears cut off in the horrific ordeal, police said.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: All five of his alleged attackers were arrested over the weekend, a move welcomed by Marx's wife and family.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: They added that the "legal process must [now] take its course".
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: The horrific attack has caused widespread outrage in a country which is used to high levels of violence.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: Police last week explained how the attack on Mark happened.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: A group of masked men armed with guns approached a worker at Mark's house as he was mowing the lawn, they said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: The attackers then demanded to know where Marx was before tying the worker's hands and feet with cable ties.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: When Marx returned home, police said two of the suspects allegedly approached him and shot him in the upper body.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: "They [then] dragged him inside the house, tied his hands and feet with cable ties, and allegedly stabbed him." The suspects then ransacked the house and took three firearms from a safe before escaping with Marx's van.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: The ordeal ended after the farm worker managed to free himself and call for assistance.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: Marx was rushed to hospital, where he remains, but may need prosthetic ears after surgeons were unable to save his own, local news site IOL reported.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: South Africa's Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp condemned the attack on Marx, adding there was no "place in our country for such senseless and barbaric acts".
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: The chair of parliament's police committee, Ian Cameron, praised police for the swift arrests and called for a "strong, properly investigated case" to follow.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: The five suspects, aged between 26 and 56, will appear in local courts on Tuesday and face house robbery, attempted murder and illegal possession of firearms and ammunition charges.
sentences.article_title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

sentences.text: Some right-wing groups have used such attacks on white farmers, who are often from the Afrikaner community, to say there is a genocide against white people in the country - a claim that has been widely discredited.

sentences.text: Although the claims have been dismissed by every political party in the country, including those representing Afrikaners, US President Donald Trump has repeated them and has offered white Afrikaners asylum in the US.

sentences.text: Uganda first deployed its troops to Somalia in 2007 Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: A first contingent of 109 Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) troops reportedly left the capital, Mogadishu, on Friday, following an announcement by Uganda's army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: Last week, Kainerugaba said Uganda had begun pulling out its troops and would hand over security responsibilities to Somali forces.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: "As we promised, we have started withdrawing UPDF from Somalia.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: After 20 years of a lot of blood and sacrifice, we are handing over security to our Somali brothers," he wrote on X.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: On Monday, Magezi said this would mark the end of Uganda's operations in the Horn of Africa country, with Somalia expected to "assume full responsibility for security".
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: The withdrawal comes after Somalia President Sheikh Mohamud met his Ugandan counterpart Yoweri Museveni in Kampala last week.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: The meeting was planned to discuss Somalia's security situation, as well as trade and economic ties between the two countries.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: The Somali president reportedly sought to persuade Uganda to extend its military presence.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: In remarks during the visit, Museveni urged Somali leaders and citizens to unite in the fight against the militant insurgency led by al-Shabab, which is part of al-Qaeda.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: An estimated 4,500 troops are in Somalia under the Africa Union mission, alongside  about 2,000 deployed through bilateral arrangements.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: Somalia has been battling a prolonged and deadly insurgency for more than two decades.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: After Ugandan forces were first deployed to the country in 2007, they played a key role in driving al-Shabab out of Mogadishu and other major towns.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: They fought alongside the Somali National Army to recapture strategic territory and secure key government installations.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: Ugandan troops were involved in successive Africa Union missions, including the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (Atmis), which began with the aim of gradually transferring security responsibilities to Somalia.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: This was replaced in 2025 by the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (Aussom), which is focused on strengthening Somalia's security institutions and preparing its forces to take full responsibility for the country's security.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: Aussom now faces uncertainty over its future funding, amid plans to wind down US and UN support.
sentences.article_title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

sentences.text: A 12-month transition plan is due to begin in January, giving Somalia and the AU time to seek alternative sources of funding.

sentences.text: El Mansouri (left) was named by King Mohammed VI (right) as the country's first female prime minister The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister.

sentences.text: Yiech Pur Biel (left) is leading the first ever refugee team at the Youth Olympics When he started running, Yiech Pur Biel had to compete barefoot.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Far from home in a new country, it was the first step towards rebuilding his life as a refugee.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: "That's when I decided now it is time to depend on myself and also to start a new life with determination," he tells BBC Newsbeat.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: In 2016, Biel made history competing in the 800m event as part of the first Olympic refugee team at the Rio summer Olympics in Brazil.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Ten years on, he's making history again leading the first refugee team for the Youth Olympics as their Chef de Mission.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Joining almost 3,000 athletes, the small team of six will be wanting to make sure their debut counts - but Biel says they're also hoping to send a message that "refugees still need our help".
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Hosted in Senegal, Saturday's opening ceremony will launch the first ever Olympic sporting event on African soil.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Africa is home to nearly 45 million displaced people, out of almost 120 million globally, representing the world's biggest displacement crisis.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Biel says for the refugee team, the Youth Olympics is "a chance for them to tell the world and also to represent the population, especially the refugee population, in Africa".
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: He ended up in Kenya, telling BBC Newsbeat: "It traumatised me, starting a new life, being alone in Kakuma," referring to the major refugee settlement close to the border between Kenya and South Sudan.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: "But I started a new life, I believe that school helped me a lot.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Doctors told the BBC about the targeting of Sudanese hospitals A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: The health minister of the group's civilian-affiliated government dismissed the allegations as propaganda.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud said it was a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: Under international law it is illegal to attack health facilities or their staff during conflict.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: The investigation also reveals the toll on medical workers in the western city.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: In the period from April 2023 to October 2025, the BBC's data shows 120 were injured, 55 killed and 10 forcibly "disappeared" or abducted.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: "The RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state," says Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who was based in el-Fasher during the siege and spoke to the BBC.

sentences.text: "The RSF started hitting these areas so citizens have no longer any way to stay there.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: It was planned." The investigation comes a year after the fall of el-Fasher, one of the most brutal chapters of the civil war which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and Sudan's military.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: Both sides have been accused of attacks on health facilities.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: El-Fasher residents had little access to healthcare during the long siege of the city In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the bombing of al-Daein hospital in RSF-held eastern Darfur, which killed dozens and forced the site to close.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: Sudan's military is believed to have carried out the drone strikes, although it has denied responsibility.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: But events in el-Fasher represent "one of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudan," the WHO said in response to a BBC query.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: UN investigators have reported that the fighting in el-Fasher bore the "hallmarks of genocide", where historical ethnic animosities have seen Arab militias - now the backbone of RSF forces - target non-Arab groups such as those that populate the city.

sentences.text: A simple guide to what is happening in Sudan Reports of mass killings in Sudan have echoes of its dark past Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say Some medical facilities in el-Fasher closed down within weeks of the country's civil war starting in April 2023.

sentences.text: Crucially this included one of the main hospitals - the Teaching Hospital - located in a conflict zone in the middle of the city.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: Its operations were moved to el-Fasher's South Hospital.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: There medical services continued, although increasingly hindered by power cuts and dwindling supplies.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: In late May and early June of 2024, the South Hospital was shelled several times as paramilitary fighters pushed forward from their positions in the east of the city.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: And they said: 'Leave him, leave him.

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: Dr Nugud, a prominent Sudanese surgeon who has joined the RSF-backed civilian government as health minister, insisted the South Hospital was being used as a military base.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: After the South Hospital shut, its staff and remaining equipment were moved to the Saudi Maternity Hospital in the west of the city, where the army had its main bases.

sentences.text: Within days the pace of attacks on the facility picked up.
sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.article_title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds

sentences.text: However, in the course of our investigation we spoke to six doctors who described a pattern of systematic targeting.

sentences.text: They told us how Saudi Hospital was repeatedly struck - on some days up to 25 times, with a mix of shelling and drones, the latter "intelligent rockets" with precision-guided attacks.

sentences.text: Smaller medical facilities also came under fire.

sentences.text: The BBC's timeline records the steady closure of private hospitals and neighbourhood clinics.

sentences.text: Lula's supporters mobilised en masse despite polls pointing to a defeat for the incumbent A WhatsApp channel created to support Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election campaign is being credited by allies with helping deliver one of the most unlikely comebacks in recent Brazilian politics.

sentences.text: Brazil's left-wing president had been trailing right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, but managed to turn the race around in just three weeks.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: At a moment when many doubted Lula could reverse the result, a WhatsApp channel called Lula's Army emerged, and rapidly grew to 10.8 million followers.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Led by Congressman André Janones, the operation encouraged supporters to share videos, promote hashtags and recruit new voters.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Its dramatic growth between the two rounds was particularly notable because it appeared to reverse a long-standing imbalance in Brazilian politics.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: For years, conservatives aligned with former President Jair Bolsonaro had been widely seen as dominating online political mobilisation, especially on platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Lula called André Janones "our General" after his major contribution paid off The emergence of Lula's Army convinced many supporters that Brazil's left had finally found a way to compete in a digital arena.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: The shift was particularly significant because social media has played a central role in Brazilian politics since Jair Bolsonaro's 2018 election victory, when WhatsApp networks became a defining feature of political campaigning.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Lula's Army messages often included ready-made templates for followers to share with friends and family.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Each one assigned supporters a specific task aimed at boosting Lula's visibility on social media.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Janones frequently instructed his "troops" to "blow up" the latest campaign video or help a new hashtag "take off".
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: "Guys, urgent!", "Don't go to sleep yet", "No food before the mission!", and "I have one more task before you're dismissed", were some of the instructions.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: The tactic worked, despite worries by some members of the Workers' Party that Janones's often-confrontational style on social media could undermine the more moderate image they hoped to project for Lula.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: In his victory speech, Lula referred to Janones as "our General" and thanked him for "raising the morale of our troops every day".
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Measuring the electoral impact of online mobilisation, however, is notoriously difficult.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: While Lula's allies credit Lula's Army with helping fuel the comeback, political scientists caution that it is impossible to determine how many votes, if any, were directly influenced by the WhatsApp operation.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Political scientist Denilde Holzhacker argues that a shift in Lula's campaign strategy was key to his comeback.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: Rather than relying solely on online engagement, she says the Workers' Party candidate succeeded in connecting digital campaigning with grassroots mobilisation on the ground.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: According to Holzhacker, the campaign intensified local efforts and adapted its messaging - linking a Bolsonaro victory with concerns about potential changes to social programmes and the loss of rights.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: "It was to Lula's credit that he recognised his own weakness and completely changed his style," she says.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: "And Janones managed to do something that had seemed unthinkable for Brazil's left - dominate social media." By contrast, Holzhacker argues that Flávio Bolsonaro entered the run-off overly confident of victory and failed to communicate his message to his supporters as effectively.

sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: "Those committed to Lula's victory worked to bring people together and persuade them to vote," Goulart says.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: She argues that the effort not only helped increase turnout but could also prove valuable for Lula's next administration.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: "I believe this collective effort was an important learning experience and will prove valuable for a government that still faces many battles ahead.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around

sentences.text: It not only helped reduce abstention, but also converted a significant number of undecided voters." Lula himself suggested that the mobilisation behind his comeback could shape the way he governs in the years ahead.
sentences.article_title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around
